title: KPI-linked Spreadsheet Heuristics and Runthrough (draft)
content:
Purpose
This is a working memo and step-by-step walkthrough for a KPI-driven cost spreadsheet that maps workload SLOs (latency & availability), request shape, and unit economics to recommended batching / caching / quantization presets. The goal: a reproducible spreadsheet and a short rubric product can adopt to auto-suggest Optimize presets for customer workloads.

Why this is different from other drafts
- Focus is on making the spreadsheet actionable as a deterministic mapping (SLO buckets -> knob suggestions) rather than just a set of heuristics.
- Includes a worked numeric example end-to-end so engineers and solutions can replicate results quickly.
- Emphasizes a small, explainable set of columns and formulas that are easy to audit and map to runtime telemetry.

Audience
- Product: build quick UI suggestions in Console.
- Solutions & SE: produce reproducible recommendations in onboarding.
- Runtime engineers: validate assumptions in profiling and telemetry.

Spreadsheet structure (recommended columns)
- workload_id: short label (chat-support-1, search-batch-embedding).
- use_case: chat | embedding | summarization | rerank | code-complete.
- p95_lat_slo_ms: numeric (SLO for 95th percentile latency in ms).
- typical_input_tokens: avg tokens in prompt.
- typical_output_tokens: avg predicted tokens.
- tokens_per_call: formula = typical_input_tokens + typical_output_tokens.
- calls_per_minute: throughput observed or expected.
- concurrency: approximate simultaneous requests (calls_per_minute / 60 * avg_latency_s).
- model_choice: (gptx-8k, opensource-13b, opensource-70b-quantized).
- per_gpu_throughput_tokens_per_s: profiling input.
- per_token_cost_usd: model-specific or negotiated price (hosted) or derived from infra costs.
- cache_prefix_hit_rate: 0-1 (manual estimate or telemetry).
- cache_kv_enabled: true/false.
- suggested_batching_mode: none | small | medium | large | adaptive.
- suggested_batch_size: numeric or formula.
- suggested_quantization: none | int8 | int4 | q5_k_dq.
- estimated_per_call_cost_usd: calculation field.
- estimated_min_latency_ms: baseline without queueing.
- estimated_p95_latency_ms: includes queuing model.
- recommended_preset_name: short text referencing preset that Console can show.

Key formulas (example forms, put into sheet cells)
- tokens_per_call = typical_input_tokens + typical_output_tokens
- baseline_infer_s = tokens_per_call / per_gpu_throughput_tokens_per_s
- concurrency = (calls_per_minute / 60) * baseline_infer_s
- if concurrency <= 1 then queue_delay_s = 0 else queue_delay_s = (concurrency - 1) * (baseline_infer_s / suggested_batching_factor)
- estimated_p95_latency_ms = (baseline_infer_s + queue_delay_s) * 1000 * latency_multiplier_for_model_and_quant (latency multiplier captures CPU/quant overhead)
- effective_tokens_per_call_after_cache = tokens_per_call * (1 - cache_prefix_hit_rate)
- estimated_per_call_cost_usd = effective_tokens_per_call_after_cache * per_token_cost_usd * quant_cost_multiplier * batching_discount_multiplier

Worked example (support chat — 50k DAU approximate on steady cadence)
- workload_id: chat-support-50k
- use_case: chat
- p95_lat_slo_ms: 300
- typical_input_tokens: 120
- typical_output_tokens: 60
- tokens_per_call: 180
- calls_per_minute: 350 (steady average)
- per_gpu_throughput_tokens_per_s: 2000 (open model profiled on T4 equivalent, FP16)
- per_token_cost_usd: 0.0000025 (hosted baseline for model variant)
- cache_prefix_hit_rate: 0.20 (20% requests short-context cache hits)

Step calculations
- baseline_infer_s = 180 / 2000 = 0.09s (90ms)
- concurrency = (350 / 60) * 0.09 = 0.525 -> <1 so queue_delay_s = 0
- estimated_p95_latency_ms ~ 90ms * latency_multiplier (1.1) => 99ms -> within 300ms SLO so we can optimize for cost.
- effective_tokens_per_call_after_cache = 180 * (1 - 0.2) = 144 tokens
- estimated_per_call_cost = 144 * 0.0000025 = $0.00036 per call

Suggested knobs (chat-support-50k)
- batching_mode: small adaptive (allow dynamic batching up to 8 requests)
- suggested_batch_size: 4 (adaptive)
- cache: prefix KV cache enabled, TTL 120s, eviction LRU by prefix frequency
- quantization: int8 (verified on model variant with negligible quality delta for this workload)
- autoscaling: keep 10% spare GPU buffer for p95 spikes, burst policy to dedicated on overflow
- recommended_preset_name: chat-interactive-lowcost-int8-smallbatch

Rationale and sensitivities
- If p95 SLO had been < 100ms we would have recommended batch_size=1 or disabled batching and prefer fp16 no-quant path.
- If cache_hit_rate < 5% then caching has little effect — rely on batching and quantization for cost.
- Quantization reduces per_token_cost_usd by quant_cost_multiplier (e.g., int8 ~ 0.6x cost, int4 ~ 0.45x) but increases baseline latency multiplier 1.05–1.25 depending on kernel maturity. Put these multipliers in a small param tab.

Preset library (compact examples)
- interactive-ultra: p95_slo_ms < 100, batching: none, quant: none, cache: optional, recommended for product-critical chat
- interactive-lowcost-int8: p95_slo_ms 100-400, batching: small-adaptive(2-8), quant:int8, cache:prefix-ON
- batch-embeddings-highthroughput: p95_slo_ms > 1000 acceptable, batching: large (256–2048 tokens per step), quant: int4/q5_k_dq, cache: disabled (not effective for embeddings), autoscale: throughput-first

How to validate against telemetry
- Telemetry inputs: observed per-request tokens, observed p95 latency, actual concurrency, cache hit_rate (from cache instrumentation), and per-model kernels used.
- Spot checks: for 10 representative customer workloads run the spreadsheet with live telemetry for last 7 days and compare estimated_per_call_cost_usd to real billing traces. Aim for estimator error < 15% across cohorts.

Runbook for SE adoption (short)
- Step 0: collect 7-day telemetry (tokens distribution, p95 latency, requests per minute).
- Step 1: load telemetry into template sheet (tab: telemetry-import).
- Step 2: run helper cells to map to SLO bucket and output recommended_preset_name.
- Step 3: sanity check: run local perf profile (per_gpu_throughput_tokens_per_s) if model variant unknown.
- Step 4: propose preset and expected monthly savings vs baseline in the sheet.

Open questions / To do
- Decide canonical multipliers for quantization latency/cost per architecture (A100/Tesla/Graviton-like CPU offload). Need profiling matrix from infra. (Action: SRE/profile team).
- Agree on a standard TTL and prefix sizing for prefix cache presets. (Action: product + runtime).
- Should the Console show a single "confidence score" from the sheet (low/medium/high) based on telemetry volume? Recommendation: yes — simple tiers: low (<1k requests/day), medium, high.
- Automate a weekly job that computes estimator error vs billing to keep multipliers up-to-date. (Action: infra + analytics).

Appendix: example compact cell formulas to copy/paste
- tokens_per_call: =C2 + D2
- baseline_infer_s: =E2 / F2
- concurrency: =(G2 / 60) * H2
- effective_tokens: =I2 * (1 - J2)
- estimated_cost: =effective_tokens * K2 * M2 * N2  // where M2 is quant multiplier, N2 batching discount

Action items (short)
- Maya: split this sheet into template + profiling param tab and upload to shared templates. (target: 2026-03-12)
- Samir: run profiler matrix for int8/int4 on top 5 model types and populate multipliers. (target: 2026-03-19)
- Jonah: wire a minimal Console UI mock using the preset names and confidence score for the onboarding flow. (target: 2026-03-26)

Notes to reviewer
- This is intentionally prescriptive to reduce back-and-forth during onboarding. Looking for pushback on assumptions (multipliers, 10% spare buffer rule, TTL defaults). Please comment in doc or ping #optimize-demos.

End of memo
